description: Two-author blind synthetic corpus: a wildlife photographer's assistant, a household renovation assistant, and a shared community-garden pool. Half the questions repeat one distinctive word from their memory; half share no content word with it. No user-derived data; frozen before any retrieval evaluation.
distractor_policy: Each query preselects one accessible non-answer seven positions later in the same pool; shared queries alternate asking scope. Each also names one inaccessible control from the other private scope.

memories.content: Remind me that the 600mm I rented from Kestrelworks has to go back by 4 March 2026, or they charge me for a full extra week.
The Sony A1 body has a hairline crack near the battery door, so I tape it before any rain outing.
Odalys Brenner at Fernline Press only wants RAW files delivered through a shared drive folder, never as email attachments.
Recap of the Svalbard trip planning: flights booked via Oslo, polar bear guard hired for six days, cold-weather batteries ordered, and the insurance rider still pending.
On 12 May 2026 the drone went down in Loch Varrin during the otter shoot; the SD card was recovered but the gimbal is dead.
I've drafted the licensing quote for the heron series at 1,800 euros for two years of web use, matching your rate from the museum deal.
Invoice TQ-4471 to the Halden Wetlands Trust covers the March bittern survey images and is due net-30.
My agent Tobias would rather get a phone call before 9am than a text whenever a shoot date moves.
Wrap-up of the Marrowind Estate commission: 42 selects delivered, two reshoots of the red deer rut scheduled, and the second payment received in full.
On 3 August 2026 my 100-400 lens was stolen from the car at a trailhead parking lot outside Brecca.
Can you add the Gitzo GT3543 tripod to the insurance schedule? It's worth about 1,100 dollars.
The studio's backup NAS sits in the hallway closet and mirrors to the cloud every night at 2am.
For the Quillon Safaris catalogue I like to shoot at f/8 and keep ISO under 3200 so the printer gets clean files.
Year-end tally for 2025: 61 paid assignments, three new editorial clients, gross income roughly 74,000 euros, and gear spending down by a fifth.
The Thornequay harbour seal shoot on 21 September 2026 was cut short when the coast guard closed the jetty for a storm warning.
Your Kenya visa is approved; the e-visa PDF is saved in the Travel folder and expires on 30 January 2027.
Pinebrook Gazette's photo desk pays a flat 275 dollars per published image, plus 40 for each online reuse.
I'd rather sleep in a cheap guesthouse close to the hide than a nice hotel an hour's drive away.
Notes from the call with Arnault Okonkwo-Reyes: he wants 12 puffin prints for the Nordvik exhibition at 60x90 cm, shipping by sea freight, deadline 15 November 2026.
Picked up the repaired Nikon Z9 from Halvard Camera Service on 2 October 2026; the shutter was replaced under warranty.
Can you remind me to call Teodor at Brightline before Friday? He still hasn't sent the revised quote for knocking out the pantry wall.
The main water shutoff valve is in the basement crawlspace behind the furnace, painted red.
Priya prefers Halden-gray grout over white for the upstairs bathroom tile, since white shows every stain.

Kitchen remodel recap as of March 14, 2026: cabinets ordered with an eight-week lead time, electrician finished rough-in, and the countertop template is scheduled once the base units are installed. Spent so far is $31,200 of the $48,000 budget.
On April 3, 2026 the city inspector signed off on the framing for permit BP-26-04417 but flagged a missing fire block near the chimney chase.
I've added Juniper's swim lessons to the family calendar: Tuesdays and Thursdays at 4:30 at the Westbrook aquatic center, starting June 9.
The dishwasher is a Klarsen DW-7740; the warranty runs through November 2027 and the appliance registration card is taped inside the junk drawer.
Daniel doesn't want any contractor working inside the house before 8 a.m. on weekdays because he takes calls from home early.

Contractor bids for the deck rebuild: Pinecrest Carpentry quoted $14,800 with composite boards, Sutter & Gale quoted $12,300 in cedar, and Hollis Brothers never returned the measurements. We're leaning toward Sutter & Gale.
Oskar broke his left wrist at the trampoline park on February 21, 2026 and wore a cast for six weeks.
The upstairs toilet keeps running after every flush again — I think the flapper is shot. Can you find a plumber who can come Saturday?
Our property tax parcel ID is 0817-QM-332, and the assessment appeal deadline each year is May 31.
Priya wants low-VOC paint in the kids' bedrooms, even if it costs more, because Juniper gets headaches from fumes.
Week of May 18 logistics: Oskar has the Quarryhill soccer tournament Saturday, Juniper's piano recital is Sunday at 2, and the Brightline crew is off Monday for Memorial Day.
The refrigerator's ice maker leaked overnight on January 12, 2026 and warped two oak floorboards; the insurance adjuster came out on January 15.
I checked the county portal: the electrical permit for the garage subpanel was issued under reference EL-5529, and it expires 180 days after issue if no inspection is requested.
Juniper is allergic to tree nuts, so her school lunches and any party snacks need to be checked for almonds and cashews.
For the new range hood, Daniel insists on venting it outside rather than a recirculating model, and he likes the Vellmar 600 CFM unit.

Insurance and warranty roundup: homeowner's policy renews September 1 with Fernbrook Mutual, the roof's workmanship warranty from Calder Roofing ends in 2031, and the water heater was replaced under warranty in 2025.
On June 27, 2026 the Brightline crew found knob-and-tube wiring behind the dining room plaster, which added a $3,450 change order.
Wren here: I've got the spare key to the Gorsemead tool shed now, so text me if you need the wheelbarrow.
Plot 6 has the waist-high beds built for wheelchair access, next to the north gate.
Marisol in bed 9 asks that nobody scatter Sproutwell slug pellets near her lettuces, even though they're labelled organic; she sticks to beer traps.
April work-day recap: compost bins turned, the rain barrel overflow pipe fixed, 30 strawberry crowns planted, and two new members signed up.
On 14 June 2026 the Larkhollow beehive swarmed and settled in the plum tree; Dev from the beekeeping club collected it that evening.
The water bill for the quarter came to 187 dollars, so each of the 22 plots owes 8.50.
The Brambleton soil test came back at pH 6.2 with low potassium, so we're adding wood ash to the east beds.
Most members voted to keep the gate unlocked during daylight hours instead of using a combination padlock.
Treasurer's update from Ilse Vandermolen: seed order 140 dollars, new hose 55, compost delivery 210, leaving 615 in the kitty.
A hard frost on 9 May 2026 killed most of the tomato seedlings that had been set out too early.
Plots 14 through 22 sit on old parking-lot fill, and the soil test showed lead at 410 ppm, so only lined raised beds are allowed there.
Has anyone got the key to the tool shed? The combination lock was swapped and I couldn't get the wheelbarrow out on Sunday morning.
The steering committee prefers that compost from the Vermillion bins go to the shared herb spiral first, before individual plots can claim any.
On August 16, 2026 the cooperative donated 212 pounds of tomatoes and zucchini to the Eastgate food pantry.
Recap of the late-summer workday: 23 volunteers turned beds, Marisol Achterberg rebuilt the drip line on the north row, the rain barrels were cleaned, and new woodchips went down on the paths.
Annual plot fees are $45 for a full bed and $25 for a half bed, due by March 1, and members on SNAP can request a waiver.
Reminder for everyone: the city water hookup at the Larkspur gate gets shut off October 31 for winter, so drain your hoses before then.
Most members want the garden kept pesticide-free, allowing only hand-picking and neem oil for pest control.
A groundhog tunneled under the east fence on July 9, 2026 and wiped out the bean row in plots 3 and 4; Tobiah Renquist set a live trap the next evening.
Fall closing checklist: pull spent plants by October 25, leave perennials in place, return borrowed tools to the shed, and cover beds with leaf mulch or cardboard.
